[[Timiș County|Timiș County Council]] | chrtitle = General director | chairman = Dinu Bara | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Dan Alexa]] | league = [[Liga II]] | season = [[2025–26 Liga III|2025–26]] | position = Liga III, Seria IV, 1st (promoted) | website = https://www.politehnicatimisoara.com/ | current = 2026–27 SSU Politehnica Timișoara season | kit_alt1 = | pattern_la1 = _sspoli2021h | pattern_b1 = _sspoli2021h | pattern_ra1 = _sspoli2021h | pattern_sh1 = _sides_on_white | pattern_so1 = | shorts1 = 5b2f89 | socks1 = FFFFFF | kit_alt2 = | pattern_la2 = _sspoli2021a | pattern_b2 = _sspoli2021a | pattern_ra2 = _sspoli2021a | pattern_sh2 = | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = 000000 | kit_alt3 = | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = }} '''Asociația Club Sportiv Știința Poli Timișoara''' ({{IPA|ro|poliˈtehnika timiˈʃo̯ara}}), commonly known as '''Politehnica Timișoara''', '''Știința Poli Timișoara''' or simply '''Poli Timișoara''', is a Romanian professional [[Association football|football]] [[Club (organization)|club]] based in [[Timișoara]], [[Timiș County]], that competes in the [[Liga II]]. Originally named ''ASU Politehnica'', the team was formed following the dissolution of the original [[FC Politehnica Timișoara]] in 2012. During that year, [[ACS Recaș]] was moved to the city and renamed [[ACS Poli Timișoara]], eventually reaching the [[Liga I|top flight]] while ''ASU'' struggled in the [[Romanian football league system|lower leagues]]. Between the two, the majority of the fans chose to support the latter, and in 2021 ACS Poli was also dissolved. That summer, the [[Politehnica University of Timișoara|Polytechnic University of Timișoara]], founder of the original team in 1921, ceded the FC Politehnica brand and records to SSU. Hence, SSU Politehnica Timișoara is the only active entity asserting the history of the original club, which has totalled 44 seasons in the top national league and won two [[Cupa României]] trophies, in [[1957–58 Cupa României|1957–58]] and [[1979–80 Cupa României|1979–80]]. The team plays its home matches in white and purple [[Kit (association football)|shirts]] at the [[Stadionul Dan Păltinișanu|Dan Păltinișanu Stadium]], which has a capacity of 32,972 seats. Their bitter rivals are [[FC UTA Arad|UTA Arad]], with whom they contest the [[West derby (Romania)|West derby]]. Another heated [[rivalry]], though somewhat smaller in scale, is with local rivals [[FC Ripensia Timișoara|Ripensia Timișoara]].{{Cite web |title=One moment, please... |url=https://www.ripensia-sport-magazin.ro/istoria-fotbalului/derby-urile-de-care-timisoara-are-nevoie/ |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20260611065951/https://www.ripensia-sport-magazin.ro/istoria-fotbalului/derby-urile-de-care-timisoara-are-nevoie/ |archive-date=2026-06-11 |access-date=2026-09-28 |website=www.ripensia-sport-magazin.ro |language=en}}"}}
